newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end mixed, Indonesian counters up.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end mixed, Indonesian counters up.

text.p: Singapore shares market ended mixed on Wednesday amid a flurry of activity in Indonesian-linked counters, dealers said.
"Market activity has been very subdued with most blue chips slightly off," said a dealer. "But there has been a bit of activity in Indonesian related counters by speculators."

Van Der Horst, ABR Holdings, Transmarco, United Pulp Paper and L&M Group were among top gainers, rising between Singapore $0.15 (US$0.11) to S$0.20 each. Some dealers said the gains came on news that two of President Suharto's children have been selected as candidates for next year's parliamentary elections.

The key Straits Times Industrials Index ended 8.72 points down at 2,102.96. Volume was at 86.72 million shares, with gainers leading losers at 174 to 133. Leading the actives were Multi-Purpose and SingTel with 4.5 million shares and 2.8 million shares respectively.
Among the losers were blue chips Fraser & Neave and City Development warrants, both shedding S$0.30 to end at S$13.90 and S$8.60 respectively.
